name: Validity of Slaughter (Shechitat Chulin)
notes: Who may slaughter, conditions under which slaughter is valid, including slaughter by deaf-mutes, minors, blind persons, on Shabbat, at night, etc.

name: Simanim (Organs Cut in Slaughter)
notes: The windpipe and gullet as the required organs to be cut in valid slaughter; rules about majority of each siman

name: Shehiyah, Derash, Chalada, Hagramah, Ikkur (Five Defects of Slaughter)
notes: The five defects that invalidate slaughter: pausing, pressing, burrowing under tissue, slanting, tearing

name: Melikah (Nipping of Bird Offerings) — Location Requirements
notes: Distinction between valid locations for melikah vs. shechitah — nape valid for melikah, throat for shechitah

name: Tereifot — Specific Conditions (Animal)
notes: Enumerated list of eighteen (or more) specific conditions making an animal a tereifa, including perforated organs, broken bones, clawing by predator, etc.

name: Tereifot — Specific Conditions (Bird)
notes: Enumerated list of conditions making a bird a tereifa, including weasel strike on head, perforated gizzard, trampling, etc.

name: Signs of Kosher Birds
notes: Rabbinic-enumerated signs for identifying kosher birds: extra digit, crop, peelable gizzard membrane; predatory behavior as disqualifier

name: Signs of Kosher Fish (Fins and Scales)
notes: Fin and scale requirements for kosher fish; debate about minimum number of scales

name: Signs of Kosher Grasshoppers
notes: Four legs, four wings, two jumping legs, wings covering majority of body; species name requirement

name: Slaughter with Idolatrous Intent
notes: Slaughter performed for the sake of idols, mountains, seas, etc. renders the animal forbidden; rules about joint slaughter with one person having forbidden intent

name: Slaughter Performed by a Gentile
notes: Gentile slaughter renders animal a neveilah; concern about idolatrous intent even when Jew intended non-sacred use

name: Ben Pekuah — Fetus Permitted by Mother's Slaughter
notes: Detailed laws of the fetus found in a slaughtered mother: when it requires its own slaughter, when it is permitted by mother's slaughter, limbs severed from fetus

name: Oto v'et B'no — Detailed Laws
notes: Detailed application of prohibition against slaughtering mother and offspring same day: combinations of sacred/non-sacred, inside/outside Temple; obligation to inform buyer; four critical days of year

name: Kisuy HaDam — Detailed Laws
notes: Detailed laws of covering blood: which animals require it, valid and invalid covering materials, blood mixtures, the koy, who is obligated

name: Gid HaNasheh — Detailed Laws
notes: Scope of prohibition (right/left thigh, fetus, non-kosher animals per R. Yehuda), how to remove it, minimum measure for lashes, cooking with meat

name: Priestly Gifts from Slaughtered Animals (Foreleg, Jaw, Maw)
notes: Obligation to give foreleg, jaw, and maw of slaughtered non-sacred animals to priests; scope, exclusions (sacrificial animals), definition of each body part

name: Reishit HaGez — Detailed Laws
notes: How many sheep trigger obligation; minimum amount of wool to give; distinction from foreleg/jaw/maw gifts; exemption if wool dyed before giving

name: Shiluach HaKen — Detailed Laws
notes: Detailed rules: which birds, domesticated vs. wild, hovering vs. resting, unfertilized eggs, fledglings able to fly, repeated return of mother, taking mother instead of sending

name: Koy (Animal of Uncertain Status)
notes: The koy is an animal of uncertain classification (domesticated or undomesticated); affects laws of kisuy hadam, firstborn, fat prohibition, and other halakhot

name: Eiver Min HaChai from a Fetus
notes: Whether a limb severed from a fetus in the womb has the status of eiver min hachai; relationship to slaughter of mother animal

name: Comparative Stringencies of Chelev and Blood Prohibitions
hebrew: חומרות חלב ודם זה לעומת זה
notes: Mishnah 8:6 lists unique stringencies: chelev of offerings is subject to meilah, piggul, notar, tumah rules; blood prohibition applies to non-kosher animals and birds

name: Basar b'Chalav — Detailed Laws (Cooking, Eating, Benefit)
notes: Whether bird meat may be cooked or placed on table with cheese; udder, heart; which meats are subject to the Torah prohibition vs. rabbinic; milk of non-kosher animal; taste imparted by drop of milk

name: Ritual Impurity of Animal Hide
notes: When animal hide retains halakhic status of flesh for impurity purposes; threshold of flaying for hide to separate from flesh status; different rules for carpet vs. jug preparation

name: Skin of Eight Creeping Animals (Sheratzim)
notes: Whether skins of the eight sheratzim impart impurity like their flesh; dispute between R. Yochanan ben Nuri and Sages; specific animals listed

name: Placenta and Edibility According to Personal Disposition
notes: Placenta found in slaughtered animal: permitted for one with hardy soul; intent to eat raises it to status of food for impurity purposes but not carcass impurity

name: Partially Severed Limb or Flesh Hanging from Animal
notes: Halakhic status of a limb or flesh that is partially severed and still attached to a living animal or person; impurity status and effect of slaughter on them

name: Darchei HaEmori (Forbidden Superstitious Practices)
notes: Prohibition against imitating Amorite superstitious practices, such as burying placenta at crossroads or hanging it on a tree to prevent miscarriage

name: Slaughter of an Animal in Mortal Danger
notes: Signs required to validate slaughter of a dying animal (convulsion of limbs, blood spurting); disputes among Tannaim

name: Nefesh HaYafah (Hardy Soul) — Concept in Kashrut
notes: Concept that items technically permitted but repulsive to most people may be eaten only by one with a hardy, undiscerning soul; applied to placenta

name: Joining of Attached Parts to Complete Egg-Bulk for Food Impurity
hebrew: צירוף עור ועצמות לביצה לטומאת אוכלין
notes: Hide, congealed gravy, spices, bones, sinews, hooves join with meat to form egg-bulk for food impurity but not for carcass impurity (olive-bulk)

name: Bones of Living Animals and Impurity
notes: Thigh bones of carcasses and creeping animals: sealed vs. perforated bones and their different impurity status for contact and carrying

name: Firstborn Animal — Laws of Consecration and Blemish
notes: Detailed rules when permanent blemish precedes consecration vs. when consecration precedes blemish: gifts of priesthood, shearing, labor, offspring, milk, slaughter outside Temple

name: Day Follows Night in Oto v'et B'no
notes: The 'one day' of the prohibition follows the night; one may slaughter by day and the offspring at night but not slaughter at night and offspring next day; derived via gezerah shavah with Creation

name: Temed (Beverage from Grape Residue) — Halakhic Status
notes: Temed before fermentation is not wine and cannot be purchased with maaser sheni money; after fermentation it is wine; effect on mikvah validity

name: Kalbon (Premium on Half-Shekel) and Animal Tithe — Partnership Rules
notes: Brothers who are partners: when obligated in kalbon are exempt from animal tithe and vice versa; rules for partners and non-partners
